summary.business: Havells is a diversified, innovation-led consumer appliances and electrical equipment company serving residential, commercial, infrastructure and industrial segments through in-house manufacturing, a wide distribution network and sustained R&D investment. Its portfolio spans switchgear, cables, lighting and fixtures, electrical consumer durables (fans, small appliances, water heaters), the Lloyd home-appliances brand (air conditioners, washing machines, refrigerators, televisions), and other emerging categories (motors, solar, pumps, water purifiers, personal grooming).

currentContext.strengths: Diversified, multi-brand portfolio (Havells, Lloyd, Havells Crabtree, Standard, REO, Havells Studio) across 24 product verticals reduces reliance on any single category|In-house manufacturing across 17 national units is viewed by the company as providing a sustainable competitive advantage through differentiation and quality control|Wide distribution reach: ~20,700 dealers and ~2.72 lakh retailers across India, plus presence in over 70 countries|Sustained R&D investment (consistently over 1% of revenue) and an 856-strong R&D team supporting a pipeline of patents and new product designs|Strong balance sheet with zero debt and a healthy cash position; long-term credit rating of AAA and short-term A1+ from CARE|Premiumisation-led brand building (e.g. Apogee switches range, IPL co-sponsorship) reinforcing brand salience across price points
currentContext.strategies: Portfolio premiumisation across categories (switchgear distribution boards, switches, fans, kitchen appliances) through differentiated, higher-value product launches|Deepening channel engagement and distribution reach via general trade, modern format retail, e-commerce/quick commerce, and expansion into semi-urban and rural markets|Reducing import dependency through supplier diversification, dual-sourcing and domestic tie-ups, aligned with 'Make in India'|In-house manufacturing and backward integration viewed as a source of differentiation and premiumisation, particularly for Lloyd (air conditioners, washing machines, refrigerators, televisions) and cables (Alwar, Tumakuru)|Expanding Lloyd from an air-conditioner-led brand into a comprehensive home-appliances brand across washing machines, refrigerators and televisions to reduce seasonality dependence|Entry into adjacent categories leveraging existing engineering strengths — Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE/EV chargers) built on switchgear, protection devices and cables capabilities|Scaling the renewables business (rooftop solar, solar pumps) with a strategic investment in Goldi Solar to secure panel/module supply and planned backward integration into domestic solar cell manufacturing|R&D-led innovation and premiumisation (e.g. CRAFT kitchen appliance series, Apogee premium switches range, high-efficiency professional luminaires) to sustain brand differentiation|Diversified geographic, channel and product-category strategy adopted deliberately to balance revenue concentration and seasonality-led volatility|For FY 2025-26, Havells confirmed payment of an already-paid Interim Dividend of Rs 4.00 per equity share and proposed a Final Dividend of Rs 6.00 per equity share (face value Rs 1 each) for shareholder approval, indicating a policy of returning cash to shareholders through a mix of interim and final dividends alongside continued reinvestment in capacity expansion. The Statutory Auditors (Price Waterhouse & Co Chartered Accountants LLP) were proposed for re-appointment for a second consecutive five-year term, reflecting continuity in audit oversight as part of the governance framework.
currentContext.expansion: Lloyd commissioned a new refrigerator manufacturing plant at Ghiloth, Rajasthan in March 2026, ahead of schedule, capable of producing Direct Cool, Frost Free, Bottom Mount and Multi-door refrigerators; the plant is IoT 4.0/MES-enabled and co-located with Ghiloth's existing air-conditioner and washing-machine manufacturing, creating an integrated multi-product appliances campus. In Cables, Havells has been accelerating capacity investment: a greenfield plant at Tumakuru was commissioned in September 2024, and further expansions are underway at both the Alwar and Tumakuru locations for domestic and export markets; during FY 2025-26 the company additionally acquired 1,58,200 square metres of land adjacent to the existing Alwar facility to support planned capacity enhancement there. Havells has invested over Rs 700 crores in Cables capacity expansion over the last two years, with further capex planned for FY 2026-27. Manufacturing capability in power cables currently extends up to 132 kV, with the company progressing towards 220 kV and higher extra-high-voltage (EHV) cables, and moving towards adoption of E-Beam (electron beam) technology to expand into railways, defence, EV charging infrastructure and data-centre cable segments; associated investments include EHV testing facilities, automation and quality laboratories. In Switches, Havells commissioned a state-of-the-art in-house paint shop at its Baddi facility during FY 2025-26. Lloyd also announced a new manufacturing line for fully automatic front-load washing machines, with the capacity expected to become operational by December 2026. Separately, Havells acquired a letter of intent from YEIDA for 50 acres of land near the new Noida International Airport, intended for future capacity expansion in consumer goods and home appliances manufacturing.
currentContext.mdna: Infrastructure- and industrial-led demand segments showed strong growth momentum during FY 2025-26 even as consumer categories were impacted by a subdued summer|GST reduction and a favourable festive season provided demand impetus to select categories|Sustained real estate activity in recent years is gradually translating into residential project completions, supporting demand for building material products|Rising demand from solar, EV charging infrastructure pickup and growing electrical-safety awareness are opening growth opportunities in switchgear|Cable demand is supported by infrastructure expansion, private sector investment, the renewable energy transition, and growth across data centres, railways, metro networks and IT sectors, though copper/aluminium price volatility creates pricing uncertainty|Continued LED price deflation is a structural headwind weighing on the lighting segment despite festive-led uptick|Nearly one-third of Havells' revenue accrues from cooling products (air conditioners, fans, air coolers, refrigerators), so a weak/short summer materially affects overall performance|The government's PM Suryaghar Yojana (target of one crore rooftop solar installations by March 2027) continues to act as a demand driver for the 'others'/solar segment|India's medium-term outlook is viewed as positive, underpinned by domestic stability and reforms (income tax relief, GST rationalisation, monetary easing) expected to gradually uplift consumer demand and discretionary spending|Global trade volatility (US tariff actions, geopolitical conflict in West Asia) and a weakening rupee are flagged as near-term uncertainties affecting commodity costs and export performance

risks.risk: Global trade volatility and geopolitical uncertainty
risks.note: FY 2025-26 was marked by US reciprocal tariff actions on several countries (including India) and the outbreak of conflict in West Asia, creating uncertainty around sourcing, logistics, demand patterns and cost structures.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility in copper and aluminium
risks.note: The Cables segment, which is Havells' largest by revenue, witnessed pronounced volatility in key input commodities (copper and aluminium), leading to pricing uncertainties across the market.
The Building Circuit Protection segment navigated a challenging environment characterised by input cost volatility and softer demand across retail and project segments.

risks.risk: Structural LED price deflation in Lighting
risks.note: FY 2025-26 continued to be another year with LED price deflation in the lighting industry, a multi-year structural headwind weighing on segment revenue and margins despite innovation efforts.

risks.risk: US tariff exposure on cable exports
risks.note: Export performance in Cables was impacted during the year due to uncertainties surrounding evolving tariff structures, particularly in the United States.

risks.risk: Rupee depreciation and elevated inflation impacting consumer demand
risks.note: Rising commodity prices and a weakening Indian rupee kept inflation elevated during the year, impacting household disposable income and consumer demand for the Company's products.

risks.risk: Seasonality and weather-dependence of consumer/cooling categories
risks.note: A subdued/weak summer impacted sales in certain consumer categories during the year, illustrating the Company's exposure to weather-driven demand volatility in cooling and consumer segments.

one-line thesis: Strong resilient top-line with **calibrated 7–8% price hikes fully passed on**, but reported profitability was deliberately dented by a **>2x YoY jump in advertising spend** (Rs 286 cr, front-loaded into Q1) that management frames as long-term brand investment and expects to normalize. The soft spots are structural-competitive: switchgear (highest-margin segment) hit by West Asia export disruption (−4% sales, −260 bps margin), and cables/wires + Lloyd ACs conceding share to peers on a distribution "sell-in → sell-out" reset. Management (as always) gives **no annual guidance** but signals stabilizing contribution margins, a Rs 1,400 cr FY27 capex, and a strategically scaling renewables business now carved out separately.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | "strong growth" (absolute not stated on call) | up | demand resilient despite RM inflation + West Asia uncertainty |
| Contribution margin | ~18.3% | broadly stable | held despite RM volatility via staggered price hikes |
| EBITDA margin | not quantified | down (A&P drag) | mgmt declined to guide EBITDA; "normalized" contribution levels ahead |
| A&P spend | Rs 286 cr | **>2x YoY** | front-loaded into Q1 (seasonal + brand reset); long-term ~2.7% of revenue |
| Switchgear | −4% YoY sales | −260 bps margin | international ~15% of switchgear; West Asia vessel disruption; normalized contribution margin 37–40% |
| Lloyd (AC) | volume +single-digit; value higher | contribution margin high-single-digit | (historically double-digit) — price hikes lifted value |
| Cables & Wires | volume ~flat (very low single-digit) | — | larger price hikes (copper/aluminium linked); sell-out reset hit end-of-qtr volumes |
> No consolidated revenue/PAT figures were given on the call (management does not present a full scorecard verbally and gives no guidance). Lighting ASP declines have stabilized with some volume growth returning. FY26 A&P was ~Rs 600 cr; FY27 could be north of Rs 700–800 cr but management anchors to **~2.7% of revenue**.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue/margin:** **no annual guidance** (long-standing policy). Qualitative: "healthy outlook on margins," expects demand to improve, contribution margins to stabilize at normalized levels; declined to commit on EBITDA margin.
- **A&P:** normalizes over the full year to **~2.7% of revenue** (Rajiv Goel); Q1 front-loading unwinds; Lloyd A&P stays elevated for "the next couple of years" (premiumization).
- **Capex FY27:** **~Rs 1,400 cr** — ~Rs 800 cr cables & wires, ~Rs 200 cr new R&D centre, remainder across other businesses.
- **Switchgear:** expects a **rebound in Q2** (international + overall) as West Asia shipping normalizes; domestic stable.
- **Lloyd contribution margin:** back to **double digits "sooner than later"** (ex the seasonally weak Q2/Q3).
- **Renewables:** margin improvement expected in **H2** (as consumer-side / inverter mix rises vs low-margin panels); no size target ("too early").
- **Price hikes:** ~7–8% average already taken (range 5–20%; cables/wires highest); most passed through, small residual into Q2.
order book & pipeline: Consumer/industrial products — no order book. Pipeline = capacity expansion (cables & wires the priority build-out), new R&D centre, and renewables adjacencies (BESS via Pixii collaboration, EV chargers, solar-cable full range). Government renewables capex is a tailwind pulling through switchgear + cables demand alongside the standalone renewables segment.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Switchgear (highest margin):** −4% YoY, −260 bps margin; ~15% international, disrupted by West Asia (no vessels) + RM volatility causing trade destocking; normalized contribution margin 37–40%; Q2 rebound expected.
- **Cables & Wires:** volume ~flat despite added capacity; management attributes to copper/aluminium volatility + a deliberate shift from "sell-in" to "sell-out" (secondary-aligned) distribution; Rs 800 cr of FY27 capex here; capacity utilization "high" but not disclosed.
- **Lloyd (ACs):** single-digit volume, higher value; delayed summer onset + BEE-rating-driven channel destock in prior quarters; contribution margin high-single-digit, targeting double-digit; A&P-heavy (top-of-mind + premiumization).
- **ECD / Lighting:** ECD absorbed price hikes; Lighting ASP stabilized, volume growth resuming, possible price hikes ahead (electronics).
- **Renewables (new segment):** scaling rapidly; Goldi Solar = strategic module supply ("strategic insourcing"); inverters in-house; panels lower-margin than inverters; focus on residential + C&I (not utility scale).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Renewables build-out** carved out as a separate segment to signal conviction: rooftop/residential + C&I solar, inverters (in-house), **BESS** (Pixii collaboration, early), **EV chargers** — leveraging brand + distribution; "can become very big."
- **Cables & wires capacity** as a multi-year share-and-volume play (Rs 800 cr FY27 capex).
- **Lloyd premiumization** via sustained A&P to build a long-term premium brand image.
- Switchgear/cables also ride the national renewables/grid capex wave as a second-order beneficiary.
margins & cost dynamics: Q1 profitability was hit by (1) the >2x A&P step-up (Rs 286 cr, deliberate brand reset + seasonal front-loading — "brand building is long-term, RM fluctuations are short-term") and (2) staggered RM inflation vs staggered price hikes creating timing gaps. Contribution margin held ~18.3%. Management expects normalized contribution margins from here as price hikes (avg 7–8%) catch up with RM; declined to guide reported EBITDA. Future margin upside framed as dual-play: operating leverage + mix shift to higher-growth categories.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY27 capex **~Rs 1,400 cr**: ~Rs 800 cr cables & wires (capacity), ~Rs 200 cr new R&D centre, balance across other businesses. Renewables capacity (Goldi) already invested last year for multi-year supply security. Watch cables capacity-ramp converting to volume (flat this quarter despite added capacity).
capital allocation: Rs 1,400 cr organic capex weighted to cables & wires + R&D; strategic renewables investment (Goldi) for supply-chain control; sustained brand investment (A&P ~2.7% of revenue) treated as long-term capital. Distribution-policy reset toward sell-out to improve channel return-on-capital. No buyback/dividend commentary on the call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Market-share erosion:** analysts repeatedly flagged Havells lagging peers in wires & cables (competitor posted high-single-digit wire / mid-single-digit cable growth; Havells ~flat) and continued AC share loss — management deflected to "sell-out reset" and long-term view.
- **Switchgear demand/geopolitics:** West Asia export disruption + trade confusion; recovery hinges on shipping normalization.
- **A&P drag persistence:** elevated Lloyd A&P for "a couple of years" caps near-term Lloyd profitability.
- **RM volatility:** copper/aluminium swings create sell-in timing distortions (dealers destock when prices fall).
- **Channel inventory** lower than normal at quarter-end for cables + ACs — could aid or distort Q2 optics.
management quality / tone: Chairman Anil Rai Gupta was confident but notably guarded — repeatedly declined guidance ("we do not give guidance for the year"), brushed off a pointed repeat question on cables/wires share loss ("I don't need to repeat my answer"), and gave a terse "I'm always confident about Havells growth." Defends the aggressive A&P timing on first-principles (long-term brand vs short-term RM noise). CFO Rajiv Goel more forthcoming on specifics (A&P at ~2.7% of revenue, capex split, renewables margin mix). Tone: long-term-oriented, disciplined on pricing, but light on hard numbers and slightly defensive on competitive share.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The profit dip is self-inflicted and deliberate** — a >2x A&P front-load (Rs 286 cr), not a demand problem; the swing factor for the rest of FY27 is A&P normalization, not top line.
- **Switchgear is the quiet worry** — it's the highest-margin segment and lost 260 bps + 4% sales; a sustained West Asia disruption matters more to profit than the volume-flat cables optics.
- **"Sell-out" distribution reset** is the recurring explanation for soft primary volumes (Havells + Lloyd both) — aligning primary to secondary should stabilize but is masking reported growth now.
- **Renewables separation is a signaling move** — management wants investors to track a business it believes "can become very big," but repeatedly refused to size it ("too early").
- Cables capacity is up yet volumes are flat — the market is watching whether the Rs 800 cr build converts, or share continues leaking to peers.

> Challenges Havells explicitly discussed: (a) West Asia export disruption in switchgear; (b) losing wires/cables + AC share to named-but-unnamed listed competitors; (c) copper/aluminium RM volatility. Mapped to listed names via our own files + sector knowledge.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "our competitor who reported a couple of days back… reported high single-digit growth in wires and low-to-mid single-digit in cables… while we are almost flat" — losing wire/cable share | **POLYCAB · 542652** ⭐; **KEI · 517569** ⭐ (wires & cables gaining share) | HAVELLS (self, ✅ flat volumes, margin dip) | Peers out-growing Havells on a high base; Havells' sell-out reset costs near-term volume; **Med** ⭐ (peers not named but clearly implied) |
| Switchgear "impacted because there are no vessels going" — West Asia export disruption | Domestic-tilted switchgear peers less export-exposed ⭐ | HAVELLS switchgear (self, −4% / −260 bps); other West-Asia-exposed exporters | Export-shipping disruption is company/geography-specific; recovery expected Q2; **Low–Med** ⭐ |
| Lloyd AC share loss + high A&P need — "market share that we're continuously losing in ACs" | **VOLTAS · 500575** ⭐; **BLUESTARCO (Blue Star) · 500067** ⭐ (AC share gainers) | Lloyd / HAVELLS (self, ✅ AC share loss) | Competitive AC market; Lloyd needs sustained A&P to defend top-of-mind; **Med** ⭐ sector-knowledge |
| Renewables scale-up (positive) — "a lot of our products, including switchgears and cables is also positively getting affected" by renewables capex | HAVELLS (self, ✅ renewables + pull-through); solar-value-chain names | — | National renewables/grid capex pulls switchgear + cables demand; **Low–Med** (self-benefit, directional) |
> RM (copper/aluminium) volatility and A&P timing are firm-specific with no external listed beneficiary to map.

capex / expansion (watch slippage): FY27 capex **~Rs 1,400 cr**: ~Rs 800 cr cables & wires (capacity), ~Rs 200 cr new R&D centre, balance across other businesses. Renewables capacity (Goldi) already invested last year for multi-year supply security. Watch cables capacity-ramp converting to volume (flat this quarter despite added capacity).
capital allocation: Rs 1,400 cr organic capex weighted to cables & wires + R&D; strategic renewables investment (Goldi) for supply-chain control; sustained brand investment (A&P ~2.7% of revenue) treated as long-term capital. Distribution-policy reset toward sell-out to improve channel return-on-capital. No buyback/dividend commentary on the call.
risks & watch-items:
- **Market-share erosion:** analysts repeatedly flagged Havells lagging peers in wires & cables (competitor posted high-single-digit wire / mid-single-digit cable growth; Havells ~flat) and continued AC share loss — management deflected to "sell-out reset" and long-term view.
- **Switchgear demand/geopolitics:** West Asia export disruption + trade confusion; recovery hinges on shipping normalization.
- **A&P drag persistence:** elevated Lloyd A&P for "a couple of years" caps near-term Lloyd profitability.
- **RM volatility:** copper/aluminium swings create sell-in timing distortions (dealers destock when prices fall).
- **Channel inventory** lower than normal at quarter-end for cables + ACs — could aid or distort Q2 optics.
management quality / tone: Chairman Anil Rai Gupta was confident but notably guarded — repeatedly declined guidance ("we do not give guidance for the year"), brushed off a pointed repeat question on cables/wires share loss ("I don't need to repeat my answer"), and gave a terse "I'm always confident about Havells growth." Defends the aggressive A&P timing on first-principles (long-term brand vs short-term RM noise). CFO Rajiv Goel more forthcoming on specifics (A&P at ~2.7% of revenue, capex split, renewables margin mix). Tone: long-term-oriented, disciplined on pricing, but light on hard numbers and slightly defensive on competitive share.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The profit dip is self-inflicted and deliberate** — a >2x A&P front-load (Rs 286 cr), not a demand problem; the swing factor for the rest of FY27 is A&P normalization, not top line.
- **Switchgear is the quiet worry** — it's the highest-margin segment and lost 260 bps + 4% sales; a sustained West Asia disruption matters more to profit than the volume-flat cables optics.
- **"Sell-out" distribution reset** is the recurring explanation for soft primary volumes (Havells + Lloyd both) — aligning primary to secondary should stabilize but is masking reported growth now.
- **Renewables separation is a signaling move** — management wants investors to track a business it believes "can become very big," but repeatedly refused to size it ("too early").
- Cables capacity is up yet volumes are flat — the market is watching whether the Rs 800 cr build converts, or share continues leaking to peers.
